---
title: "Joins"
number-depth: 2
format: 
    html:
        code-fold: false
---

A **join** takes two tables and stitches them into one, based on some matching condition. Think of it as a Cartesian product (every row paired with every row) that's then *filtered* down to only the pairs that actually make sense together.

Every join (except cross join) is a **join type** plus a **join condition**:

```{=html}
<div class="flow"><div class="box"><b>Join type</b><span>which rows are kept</span></div><div class="arrow">+</div><div class="box grey"><b>Join condition</b><span>which rows match</span></div></div><div class="flow-label">Join types</div><div class="flow"><div class="box"><b>inner</b><span>matching rows only</span></div><div class="box"><b>left outer</b><span>+ unmatched left rows</span></div><div class="box"><b>right outer</b><span>+ unmatched right rows</span></div><div class="box"><b>full outer</b><span>+ unmatched rows of both</span></div></div><div class="flow-label">Join conditions</div><div class="flow"><div class="box grey"><b>natural</b><span>all same-named columns</span></div><div class="box grey"><b>using (A, ...)</b><span>only the listed columns</span></div><div class="box grey"><b>on &lt;predicate&gt;</b><span>any condition</span></div></div>
```

---

## Sample Data

The joins on this page use small relations from the three course datasets. Run each block to see the rows that will be joined.

**University:** the courses offered in Fall 2009 and the courses offered in Spring 2008. Run this block once to create them as two views, then look at them:

```{.sql db="university"}
create or replace view fall_2009 as
    select distinct s.course_id, c.title
    from section as s join course as c on s.course_id = c.course_id
    where s.semester = 'Fall' and s.year = 2009;

create or replace view spring_2008 as
    select distinct course_id, building
    from section
    where semester = 'Spring' and year = 2008;

select * from fall_2009;     -- 7 courses
select * from spring_2008;   -- 9 courses
```

Only course `237` is in both: 6 Fall courses have no Spring match, and 8 Spring courses have no Fall match. This mismatch is exactly what different join types handle differently.

**LIS:** faculty, and the library members who are faculty:

```{.sql db="lis"}
select id, faculty_fname, faculty_lname from faculty;
select member_no, id from members where member_class = 'Faculty';
```

**FLIS:** the teams and the referees:

```{.sql db="flis"}
select team_id, name from teams;
select referee_id, name from referees;
```

---

## Cross Join

Returns the **full Cartesian product** — every row of one table paired with every row of the other, no filtering at all.

```{.sql db="university"}
-- Explicit
select * from fall_2009 cross join spring_2008;

-- Implicit (comma syntax)
select * from fall_2009, spring_2008;
```

With 7 Fall courses and 9 Spring courses, this produces **63 rows** — almost all of them meaningless pairings.

The same on another dataset: every team paired with every referee (6 × 7 = 42 rows):

```{.sql db="flis"}
select count(*)
from teams cross join referees;
```

---

## Inner Join

Keeps only the rows where the join condition is satisfied on **both sides**.

| Join Type | Condition | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **Equi-Join** | Explicit equality condition (`on a.x = b.x`) | Both `x` columns kept |
| **Natural Join** | Equality assumed on same-named columns | Duplicate column auto-dropped |

```{.sql db="university"}
-- Equi-join (course_id appears twice)
select * from fall_2009 inner join spring_2008
on fall_2009.course_id = spring_2008.course_id;

-- Natural join (same row, but course_id appears once)
select * from fall_2009 natural join spring_2008;
```

Only course `237` survives. The other Fall and Spring courses all **disappear** — this is the information loss outer joins solve.

```{=html}
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>course_id</th><th>title</th><th>building</th><th>what happens</th></tr><tr><td>237</td><td>Surfing</td><td>Power</td><td>in both: kept</td></tr><tr><td>105</td><td>Image Processing</td><td>–</td><td>no Spring match: dropped</td></tr><tr><td>158</td><td>–</td><td>Taylor</td><td>no Fall match: dropped</td></tr></table></div>
```


---

## Outer Join

Outer joins keep the inner join result **plus** the unmatched rows from one or both sides, filling missing columns with `null`.

```{=html}
<div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>1 · inner join</b></div><span>matching rows</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>2 · add unmatched</b></div><span>from the left, right or both</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>3 · fill</b></div><span>missing columns with null</span></div></div>
```

### Left Outer Join

Keeps **all rows from the left table**, even unmatched ones.

```{.sql db="university"}
select * from fall_2009 natural left outer join spring_2008;
```

All 7 Fall courses are kept; the 6 with no Spring match get `null` for `building`.

```{=html}
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>course_id</th><th>title</th><th>building</th></tr><tr><td>237</td><td>Surfing</td><td>Power</td></tr><tr><td>105</td><td>Image Processing</td><td><span style="color:var(--dbms-muted)"><i>null</i></span></td></tr><tr><td>242</td><td>Rock and Roll</td><td><span style="color:var(--dbms-muted)"><i>null</i></span></td></tr><tr><td>…</td><td></td><td></td></tr></table></div>
```


The same on another dataset: every faculty member with their library member number. The faculty member who is not a library member is kept, with `null`:

```{.sql db="lis"}
select f.faculty_fname, f.faculty_lname, m.member_no
from faculty as f left outer join members as m
on m.id = f.id;
```

### Right Outer Join

Keeps **all rows from the right table**, even unmatched ones.

```{.sql db="university"}
select * from fall_2009 natural right outer join spring_2008;
```

All 9 Spring courses are kept; the 8 with no Fall match get `null` for `title`.

```{=html}
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>course_id</th><th>title</th><th>building</th></tr><tr><td>237</td><td>Surfing</td><td>Power</td></tr><tr><td>158</td><td><span style="color:var(--dbms-muted)"><i>null</i></span></td><td>Taylor</td></tr><tr><td>345</td><td><span style="color:var(--dbms-muted)"><i>null</i></span></td><td>Taylor</td></tr><tr><td>…</td><td></td><td></td></tr></table></div>
```


The same on another dataset: every department with its instructors, including the departments that have none:

```{.sql db="university"}
select dept_name, id, name
from instructor natural right outer join department;
```

### Full Outer Join

Keeps **everything from both sides** — the union of left and right outer joins.

```{.sql db="university"}
select * from fall_2009 natural full outer join spring_2008;
```

1 matched course + 6 Fall-only + 8 Spring-only = **15 rows**.

```{=html}
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>course_id</th><th>title</th><th>building</th><th>came from</th></tr><tr><td>237</td><td>Surfing</td><td>Power</td><td>both</td></tr><tr><td>105</td><td>Image Processing</td><td><span style="color:var(--dbms-muted)"><i>null</i></span></td><td>Fall only</td></tr><tr><td>158</td><td><span style="color:var(--dbms-muted)"><i>null</i></span></td><td>Taylor</td><td>Spring only</td></tr><tr><td>…</td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr></table></div>
```


### Using Explicit Conditions

Joins can also use `on` (any condition) or `using` (shared column names), instead of `natural`:

```{.sql db="university"}
-- Explicit condition
select * from fall_2009 left outer join spring_2008
on fall_2009.course_id = spring_2008.course_id;

-- Shared column shorthand
select * from fall_2009 full outer join spring_2008
using (course_id);
```

::: {.callout-note title="Key idea"}
`on` works with *any* condition (even inequality!). `natural` and `using` both rely on matching column names — `using` lets you name exactly which shared column(s) to join on, while `natural` matches on **all** identically-named columns.
:::

---

## Quick Reference: Join Types

| Join | Unmatched left rows kept? | Unmatched right rows kept? |
|---|:---:|:---:|
| Cross Join | n/a (no matching) | n/a |
| Inner Join | ✗ | ✗ |
| Left Outer | ✓ | ✗ |
| Right Outer | ✗ | ✓ |
| Full Outer | ✓ | ✓ |
